A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRAM research work. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRAM experiments on response ranking, PPO fine-tuning, and reward-model adaptation, together with scaling studies and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark accuracies, PPO win rates, adaptation curves, and ablations in the appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions use identical response-pair pretraining, supervised preference generation with label smoothing, and reference-based scoring and ranking procedures. No algorithm, objective, architecture, or inference component changes.

E1.justification: Unified-Feedback, RewardBench, HHH-Alignment, Alpaca/AlpacaFarm/AlpacaEval2, and summarization and harmlessness adaptation coverage are unchanged. The appendices introduce no different datasets or task scenarios in v3.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same LLM-as-a-Judge, open-source reward-model, and trained discriminative/generative comparators. The comparator sets in the PPO, adaptation, and appendix comparisons also match.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–D retain the same model sizes, data splits and sample counts, training budgets, metrics, BoN sampling procedures, PPO settings, and adaptation protocols.

E4.justification: The data-scaling and domain analyses in Section 5, two-stage ablations and label-smoothing studies in Appendix D, and PPO case studies in Tables 6–7 are retained without additions or revisions.

E5.justification: The plotted error bars and statistical reporting are unchanged. No run counts, seeds, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative cases match throughout. For example, Table 1 retains GRAM RewardBench averages of 85.1 and 83.6 for the 8B and 3B models, while Table 3 retains GRAM win rate 12.63 and length-controlled win rate 11.12.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives are unchanged, including the two-stage training derivation in Appendix A and the label-smoothing/Bradley-Terry derivation in Section 3.3 and Appendix D.2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: learning from unlabeled and labeled data, connecting generative training to regularized pairwise ranking, and improving reward generalization and adaptation.

C2.justification: The explanations of generalization, overoptimization, domain effects, freezing, and label smoothing remain unchanged. No substantive limitations, applicability qualifications, or mechanism interpretations are added or removed.

D1.justification: The code links on page 1 and in Section 7 change from wangclnlp/GRAM/tree/main to NiuTrans/GRAM. The same Hugging Face collection link is relabeled from Models to Datasets&Models. These update access information; implementation details remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish a new resource release.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list, and research positioning remain unchanged, including Section 6 and Appendix A's positioning of pretraining preference features from unlabeled data.

P1.justification: The front-page resource label changes from Models to Datasets&Models, alongside the version/date stamp. Scientific prose, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 8's panel-group labels change from (c)/(d) to (a)/(b), while its curves, axes, and legend remain unchanged. Resource-header spacing and conclusion line wrapping also change slightly; no figures or tables are added, removed, or relocated.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, theory, empirical evidence, and interpretations are unchanged throughout both PDFs and their appendices. Corrected Figure 8 lettering and resource-link edits provide slight editorial polish, but the PDFs do not establish improved resource availability. These maintenance changes do not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
